# The Dark Between the Stars

## Scripture

*"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit."* — Psalm 147:4–5 (NIV)

## Reflection

On a clear October night, far from city lights, you may notice something easy to miss: the sky isn't solid black. Between the stars lies a faint, milky glow—the combined light of billions of distant suns too far to distinguish individually. Astronomers call it the integrated starlight. Even the darkness is full of light we simply cannot see.

How like our seasons of waiting. When God seems silent, when prayers feel unanswered and the night stretches long, we assume nothing is happening. But Scripture tells us God numbers the stars and calls each one by name—not one is forgotten, not one drifts beyond His attention. The light is still there, even when our eyes can't separate it from the dark.

Perhaps your current season feels like that faint glow: no bright, obvious sign, just the quiet sense that something is holding you. That something is Someone. The God who names every star knows your name too. He has not lost track of you in the vastness. The darkness between the stars is not empty—it is filled with light too great to see all at once. So is the space where you're waiting.

## Prayer

Lord, when the night feels empty, remind me that Your light fills even the spaces I cannot see. You call every star by name—thank You for calling mine. Give me patience in the waiting and trust in Your unseen faithfulness. Amen.
